title: 40 Years Ago, Oceanographers Found the Wreckage of the RMS Titanic - Nautilus
gist: Marking the 1985 discovery of the RMS Titanic wreck by oceanographers Jean-Louis Michel and Robert Ballard, the piece recounts how the pair located the wreck 73 years after the sinking by tracking a debris trail rather than relying on sonar.

insights.claim: Oceanographers Jean-Louis Michel and Robert Ballard discovered the wreckage of the RMS Titanic in September 1985, 73 years after it sank, with the wreck located roughly 12,500 feet underwater and about 370 miles from the coast of Canada.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A precise historical benchmark (depth, distance, timeline) useful for context in any deep-sea exploration or maritime-archaeology discussion.

insights.claim: Sonar scanning failed to locate the Titanic wreck, so Michel and Ballard instead searched for the wider debris field that had spilled from the ship, correctly reasoning it would cover far more area than the intact wreck itself, and located the ship's boiler after a week of searching before following the debris trail back to the hull.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: The 'search for the debris field, not the target' technique became a foundational methodology in deep-sea wreck hunting, applicable to later searches for other lost vessels or aircraft.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning "Finding the long-lost ship wasn’t a simple task"
